the disowning-gate arm driven to a refused revert, beside the existing blamesSpan cases

summary: A refused afterMerge revert blames its entry unconditionally, so a gate declaring `blamesSpan: false` still quarantines that entry for the run
acceptance: an afterMerge gate that declares `blamesSpan: false` and whose revert is then refused leaves a gate-stage failure carrying neither `tag` nor `quarantineKey`, so the run-scoped quarantine holds no entry for a bystander collision the gate said its span did not build — while a gate that declared no attribution still reports both halves, and the attribution is read at one site for the gate failure and both refusal legs rather than spelled per leg
tests: a revert refused after a gate declaring blamesSpan false records an unblamed gate failure
notes: Verified on disk: `src/waveMerge.ts:865` reads `entryFailure.blamesSpan === false`; the refusal legs at `:896` and `:919` push `...blamedOn(r.entry)` unconditionally, and any tagged failure quarantines for the run (`src/loopSupervisor.ts:788`). `revertAfterCommitFailure` (`src/tickAttempt.ts`) already honors it, and `src/singletonTick.ts` spells one `mergeFate` where the wave copies the leg. Repro: `blamesSpan: false` on the collide-veto gate at `tests/Dispatcher.test.ts:8548`.
